ratings_why.fun: Every tier has a job, the Burrow is a pile you grow, guard and spend every turn, and the late game has big in-fight payoffs to aim for.
ratings_why.distinct: A token swarm is familiar, but an off-board reserve that is fight HP, ammunition and currency at once plays unlike today's tribes.

verdict_why: "Your front unit" needs a definition, and Kit size has too few cards to keep the Kits relevant late.

points.text: The Front Lemming and Brother Onward both say "your front unit" with no definition: is it F1 only, or your first living unit in reading order? Define it once as a keyword.
Only Tunic Weaver and Old Mother Lemen raise Kit size, so Kits stay 2/2 to 3/3 while late boards reach 30/30. A Tier 3 or 4 card that grows Kit size each turn would give the size axis a real curve.
Herding Council gives about 8 stats a turn for 2 Kits, low for Tier 4. Let it spend up to 6 Kits, +1/+1 per pair.
The Burrow has no cap, so by the late game it can hold 40 or more Kits and fights get long. A visible cap that rises with your tier would keep fights readable without cutting the power.
Identical Cousin copies a Tier 6 unit at Tier 4 and builds triples. That's a fun high roll; say whether the copy is ever golden.

standouts.why: Herald of the Lemenår doubles the Burrow under a cap: a clear Tier 5 direction card that tells you to build the Tide.
Brother Onward's growing Banner fits the seed and gives the Kit chain a big late payoff you can see.
Raft-builder lets a Tier 3 cash in the Burrow early, and makes keeping Kits back a decision.

weakest.why: Herding Council's output is under Tier 4's target, and Ferrywife does the same job better.
Ole the Learned's damage follows Kit Attack, which barely grows, so it fades after the midgame.
Tunic Weaver is nearly the only permanent Kit-size card, so it's a must-have early and the axis ends with it.

flags.note: Herald with Litter Keeper makes about 10 Kits a turn, and the Burrow never drains in fights, so fight HP keeps piling up.
With Herald refilling the Burrow, Ferrywife can give each real unit +8/+8 or more a turn, and a golden one doubles it.
Cantor with a 30-Kit Onward chain makes the biggest unit huge within one fight.
With Old Mother Lemen pouring Kits into the front, the Banner can pass 20 or more times and reach +80/+80.
An uncapped Burrow with Onward, Bristle and low-Attack Kits could cause long fights and many ties.
